<validation_instructions>
  You are validating an instrument grounding result. This is a discrimination task - determine if the match makes sense.

  <validation_criteria>
  VALIDATION CRITERIA (ALL must pass):
    <criterion>Name/Type alignment: Do instrument names/types align reasonably?</criterion>
    <criterion>Mission reference match: Do mission references match (if specified)?</criterion>
    <criterion>Temporal compatibility: Are time periods compatible (if specified)?</criterion>
    <criterion>Scientific capability match: Can the matched instrument actually perform the described observations?</criterion>
    <criterion>Domain consistency: Are mission and instrument scientifically compatible with described context?</criterion>
  </validation_criteria>

  <critical_rules>
  CRITICAL VALIDATION RULES:
    <rule>Cross-domain mismatches are INVALID: Solar data descriptions → Space station instruments = INVALID</rule>
    <rule>Capability mismatches are INVALID: Cosmic ray detector → "solar data collection" = INVALID</rule>
    <rule>Spacecraft variant errors are INVALID: STEREO-A description → STEREO-B match = INVALID</rule>
  </critical_rules>

  <examples>
    <invalid>"ISS solar data collection" → ISS AMS-02 (AMS-02 is cosmic ray detector, not solar instrument)</invalid>
    <invalid>"GOES-13 SEM" → GOES-12 SXI (wrong satellite + wrong instrument type)</invalid>
    <invalid>"XRI magnetospheric" → FOXSI solar imager (wrong mission focus)</invalid>
    <invalid>"STEREO-A EUVI" → STEREO-B EUVI (wrong spacecraft variant)</invalid>
    <valid>"BARREL XRI" → BARREL 1J XRI (specific instance of generic reference)</valid>
    <valid>"GOES Space Environment Monitor" → GOES-13 SEM (reasonable specific match)</valid>
    <valid>"GOLF helioseismology" → SOHO GOLF (scientific capability matches)</valid>
  </examples>

  First provide detailed reasoning addressing each validation criterion, then conclude with:
  **CONCLUSION: VALID** or **CONCLUSION: INVALID**
</validation_instructions>

<validation_task>
  <original_description>
    <name>GOLF (Global Oscillations at Low Frequencies) on board SOHO</name>
    <context>GOLF velocity time-series were analyzed to extract individual p-mode energies (the "superficial" energy per unit mass at the solar surface). The primary dataset is a continuous 310-day GOLF run near solar minimum; Fourier filtering with a window of 8 Hz (≈1.45 day time resolution) was used to isolate modes n=17–25, l=0 and 1. A one-day instrument stop on 1996-09-08 was handled by removing four days of signal around instrument stabilization for the statistical analysis.</context>
    <time_info>Time period: 1996-04-11 to 1997-02-14</time_info>
    <observation_info>Observes: Oscillatory surface velocity and the "superficial" energy per unit mass E(t) of individual p-modes</observation_info>
  </original_description>

  <proposed_match>
    <instrument>Global Oscillations at Low Frequencies (GOLF)</instrument>
    <mission>Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO)</mission>
  </proposed_match>

  <instruction>
    Evaluate this match against all validation criteria. First provide detailed reasoning addressing each criterion, then conclude with:
    **CONCLUSION: VALID** or **CONCLUSION: INVALID**
  </instruction>
</validation_task>

  <original_description>
    <name>IPHIR</name>
    <context>Previously published IPHIR photometric/velocity measurements (a 160-day run at the end of 1988) were re-analyzed with the paper's energy-extraction method and statistical tests for comparison with GOLF results. Due to higher noise level in IPHIR, the filtering window was limited to 6 Hz (time resolution ≈ 1.9 days), and gaps in the series (around day 5 and day 61) led to removing surrounding data and shortening the usable sample to 78 points.</context>
    <time_info>Time period: 1988-08-24 to 1988-12-31 (160 days at the end of 1988; exact start/end not explicitly given in text — interval inferred as the final 160 days of 1988)</time_info>
